mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production and housing starts both increase, it indicates economic expansion, boosting S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by 1% and HOUST increases by 50k
failure_condition: If both indicators increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate during tightening cycles may negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer prices may lead to inflation, negatively affecting S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: If CPI increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% in the next 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: Significant payroll employment growth signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS grows by 50k but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate and low unemployment indicate a positive economic environment, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 30%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts in an early-cycle expansion signals economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by 50k but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40%.
